RE: Member ID: CCH-30092251

Patient: Priya Nandakumar  
Service: Infliximab infusion  
Date of Service: September 13, 2026, September 27, 2026, October 11, 2026  

Dear Appeals Coordinator,

This letter constitutes a formal first-level appeal of the denial for claim number 2026-PA-118734, dated October 26, 2026, which stated: "This claim has been denied because prior authorization was not obtained before the services were provided, as required for specialty infusion medications."

Under Section 5.2 Prior Authorization of the Cascade Community Health Plan policy, retrospective authorization will be granted when the service would have been approved had prior authorization been requested and the provider submits documentation within 90 days of the date of service. The Infusion Center Note dated September 8, 2026 confirms that a prior authorization request was faxed to Cascade on September 8, 2026 (confirmation #F-882173), five days before the first infusion on September 13, 2026. This demonstrates timely submission of the request prior to service, satisfying the condition for retrospective review.

Furthermore, the patient meets the coverage criteria for infliximab under Section 6.1 Crohn's Disease Biologic Therapy, which states that infliximab is covered for moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease after an inadequate response to, or intolerance of, at least one conventional therapy. The Gastroenterology Note from Dr. Helen Park dated September 6, 2026 documents that Priya Nandakumar failed azathioprine from 2020 to 2022 due to hepatotoxicity and has been on infliximab 5 mg/kg every eight weeks since 2023 under her prior insurer, Evergreen Health, with sustained remission. This confirms she satisfies the clinical requirements for coverage.

Additionally, Section 5.3 Continuity of Care provides that members who were receiving an ongoing course of treatment under a previous health plan at the time of enrollment may continue that treatment for up to 90 days while prior authorization is obtained. The same Gastroenterology Note confirms Priya was receiving ongoing infliximab therapy under Evergreen Health at the time of her enrollment in Cascade, effective August 13, 2026. The infusions in question—September 13, September 27, and October 11, 2026—fall well within the 90-day continuity-of-care window, during which Cascade is obligated to allow continuation of treatment while pursuing authorization.

Given that the provider submitted the prior authorization request before service, the patient meets all clinical criteria for coverage, and the treatments fall within the continuity-of-care protection period, the denial based on lack of prior authorization is inconsistent with the plan’s own policies. I request that Cascade Community Health Plan immediately overturn this denial, authorize and pay for the infliximab infusions administered on September 13, September 27, and October 11, 2026, and expedite processing of any outstanding prior authorization.

Due to the risk of disease flare and antibody formation associated with interruption of biologic therapy, I also request an expedited peer-to-peer review between Dr. Helen Park and a Cascade medical director, as permitted under Section 10.1 Appeals for cases where delay could seriously jeopardize the member’s health.

Please provide a full copy of the claim file, including all criteria used in the denial decision, within the required timeframe.

Respectfully,  

Priya Nandakumar
